original.label: tab:rouge_tradeoff
original.caption_excerpt: Category B Lexical Alignment and Answer Verbosity Trade-off.

equivalent_source_candidates.text: ROUGE-L F1 penalizes length through candidate-length precision ($\text{LCS}/|\text{cand}|$), and the reference holdings average $70.8$ words (computed against researcher-constructed references, \texttt{terra\_350\_benchmark.json}, SHA256 \texttt{8144fa81...}, by deterministic tokenized LCS; F1 is the mean of per-query F1, not the harmonic mean of the macro P and R). On Category~B, Flat Vector RAG has the highest F1 ($\mathbf{\FlatRAGCatBRougeFOne}$ vs.\ TERRA $\TerraCatBRougeFOne$, HippoRAG $\HippoRAGCatBRougeFOne$, GraphRAG $\GraphRAGCatBRougeFOne$, Direct LLM $\DirectLLMCatBRougeFOne$) and precision ($\mathbf{\FlatRAGCatBRougePrecision}$ vs.\ TERRA $\TerraCatBRougePrecision$, HippoRAG $\HippoRAGCatBRougePrecision$, GraphRAG $\GraphRAGCatBRougePrecision$, Direct LLM $\DirectLLMCatBRougePrecision$), because TERRA writes longer chronological syntheses (mean words in Table~\ref{tab:cat_b_performance}). On recall, TERRA's firewall falsely refuses \TerraCatBFalseRefusals\ Category~B queries (scored zero), giving $\TerraCatBRougeRecall$ against $\FlatRAGCatBRougeRecall$ (Flat), $\GraphRAGCatBRougeRecall$ (GraphRAG), $\HippoRAGCatBRougeRecall$ (HippoRAG) and $\mathbf{\DirectLLMCatBRougeRecall}$ (Direct LLM); on answered queries TERRA reaches \TerraCatBAnsweredRougeRecall\ (mean \TerraCatBAnsweredMeanWords\ words), comparable to Flat's \FlatRAGCatBAnsweredRougeRecall. N-gram overlap cannot separate valid modern doctrine from overruled precedent, since it rewards verbatim citation of dead law; TERRA's strengths lie in verified citation-graph recovery (Table~\ref{tab:retrieval_eval}) and dual-judge faithfulness ($\TerraCatBFaithfulness$, FDR $q < 0.05$).
